title: Web application firewall (WAF) and reverse proxy

videos.script: The shop's application never talks to the internet. A proxy in the DMZ does it on its behalf. {{proxy}} In this lesson you will follow one request through two connections, and see what each machine writes down about who asked. {{logs}} Then the proxy starts refusing things. Methods the shop never uses. Bodies too big for any of its forms. Admin pages, to everybody outside the office. {{refuse}} Then a rate limit, which caps how fast one address may ask. Thirty requests go in, and some come back as too many. {{limit}} Last, a web application firewall. It reads each request for the patterns of known attacks. You will run it first in a mode where it only watches, then let it block. And you will watch it refuse a customer who did nothing wrong, and fix that without switching it off. {{waf}}
